analysis.title: Oracle Corp. Three Points For OCRL's FAD
key_insights: Oracle hosts its analyst day on Wednesday alongside its annual customer conference (Oracle AI World). Barclays is looking for incremental information on three items: FY28 funding needs, a possibly updated approach to long-term guidance, and the health of the AI story.

Oracle is shifting from a database vendor with a sizable applications business toward a major AI compute provider. The executive leadership team has been completely replaced since last year, and this is the last event for long-standing Head of Investor Relations Ken Bond.
The new team's main job at the analyst day is to reassure investors given uncertainty in the AI market, especially for players relying more on debt financing (CRWV, ORCL).

Last quarter was almost a 'perfect quarter' for Oracle: better revenue, solid underlying profitability, and confirmation that FY27 financing is well supported, including the $20bn equity raise over the summer. The shares still did not react well.
Long-only investors' main pushback is that FY28 capex requirements could start another heavy round of funding needs. Any incremental information at the analyst day would help.

Barclays rebuilt its model to capture capex and financing needs. It sees capex of $94bn in FY27 and $103bn in FY28 versus consensus of $84bn and $107bn. It has ORCL turning unlevered FCF positive in FY29, with lower cash burn than consensus in FY27 and FY28.

The previous management team gave long-term guidance as point estimates, with specific dollar targets for revenue and EPS through FY30. Barclays says this 'handcuffs' management to specific numbers and wants to see how the new CFO approaches the outlook.

A shift in go-live dates for large data center projects can move the dollar targets. The large New Mexico project, currently in headlines over permitting, is expected to contribute meaningfully in FY28 and more in FY29, so each delay headline can weigh on the shares.

Barclays says Oracle takes a portfolio approach to projects, so a delay in one does not derail the broader growth story. Even without New Mexico, Oracle should still grow revenue and EPS at a very healthy rate. Barclays has no new information suggesting that outcome.
Point-based guidance also prevents Oracle from establishing the beat-and-raise cadence that software stocks typically need to work.

On AI, Barclays expects management to cover the large compute contracts with model companies such as OpenAI (private, not covered) and Meta, plus internal AI efforts in Fusion and NetSuite and keeping the Oracle database relevant. Several announcements are expected at Oracle AI World.
Barclays rates ORCL Overweight with a $252 price target (about 26x CY27E P/E on CY27E EPS of $9.71), versus a $126.16 close on 23-Oct-2026, implying +99.7% upside.

market_movers.rationale: Barclays keeps Overweight ahead of the analyst day. The target rests on about 26x CY27E P/E and CY27E EPS of $9.71, implying +99.7% upside from $126.16.

sector_views.rationale: Barclays' industry view for U.S. Software is Positive, and ORCL is rated Overweight within it.

earnings_insights: Last quarter (reported, not specified further) Oracle had better revenue, solid underlying profitability and confirmed FY27 financing, including the $20bn summer equity raise. Barclays called it almost a 'perfect quarter', but the shares did not react well.
Barclays forecast: capex $94bn FY27 and $103bn FY28, versus consensus $84bn FY27 and $107bn FY28.
Barclays forecast: ORCL turns unlevered FCF positive in FY29, with lower cash burn than consensus in FY27 and FY28.
Barclays price target of $252 uses CY27E EPS of $9.71 (Barclays estimate) at about 26x P/E.
risk_factors: FY28 capex could trigger another heavy round of funding needs.
Delays in large data center projects, such as New Mexico (permitting), could hurt FY28 and FY29 targets and weigh on the shares.
Point-estimate long-term guidance constrains management and prevents a beat-and-raise cadence.
Heavy reliance on debt financing for the AI build-out creates credit risk, particularly if a large customer fails.
Competition in SaaS and IaaS could lower overall growth, and the core database could lose share to other hyperscaler offerings and non-relational solutions.
Uncertainty in the AI market, especially for debt-financed players (CRWV, ORCL).

tension_points.bull_case: Barclays models capex of $103bn in FY28 (below consensus $107bn) and unlevered FCF turning positive in FY29, with lower cash burn than consensus in FY27 and FY28. FY27 financing is confirmed, including the $20bn equity raise.
tension_points.bear_case: Long-only investors worry that FY28 capex requirements could start another heavy round of funding needs, and the shares did not react well to a near-perfect quarter.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management commentary at the analyst day showing FY28 funding needs larger than expected would undercut the case. Barclays gives no specific numeric threshold.
